_comment: Central assessment registry (docs/AUDIT.md section H, item 1). Subject -> Unit -> Topic -> Assessment. This file is the STATIC FALLBACK and seed: when Firebase is configured the live registry lives in Firestore and this file is what seeds it, and on plain static hosting (GitHub Pages, python -m http.server) it is read directly so the app keeps working with no backend at all. Teachers add subjects/units/assessments through teacher.html, which writes Firestore and can re-export this file — editing JavaScript is never required to add one. Schema and validation: lib/assessmentRegistry.js.

subjects.name: Generative AI and Large Language Models

units.name: Unit I
units.title: Fundamentals of Generative AI and Large Language Models
units._comment_legacy: legacy_unit_key maps this unit back to the bare roman numeral stored on every question in data/questions-unit1.json (q.unit === 'I') and used as the keywordBanks/{unit} document id. It is what lets a registry-driven assessment reuse an existing committed bank unchanged. New units created from uploaded material do not need it.

course_outcomes.description: Explain the foundations of generative AI and large language models.

assessments.title: CSA65 Unit I — Fundamentals of Generative AI and LLMs
assessments._comment_legacy: legacy_quiz_id keeps this assessment's localStorage progress/timer keys and its Firestore submission document ids identical to the ones data/config-unit1-quiz1.json already produces, so an in-progress attempt started before the registry existed is not orphaned by the migration.
